target: tracker.sh restore — refuses a spec that was never shelved
cmd:
mkdir -p factory/specs; printf -- '---
id: 001
title: normal
status: specd
---
body
' > factory/specs/001-a.md; printf -- '---
id: 002
title: no-provenance
status: shelved
---
body
' > factory/specs/002-b.md; source "$PLUGIN_ROOT/scripts/lib/tracker.sh"; if ( tracker_restore factory/specs/001-a.md me ) >/dev/null 2>&1; then A=0; else A=$?; fi; if ( tracker_restore factory/specs/002-b.md me ) >/dev/null 2>&1; then B=0; else B=$?; fi; jq -n --argjson a "$A" --argjson b "$B" --arg s1 "$(_tracker_field factory/specs/001-a.md status)" --arg s2 "$(_tracker_field factory/specs/002-b.md status)" '{a: $a, b: $b, s1: $s1, s2: $s2}'
_note: two ways restore must refuse: not shelved at all, and shelved with no shelved_from (a hand-edited file). Guessing a destination is worse than refusing — it would silently reinsert a spec at the wrong stage.
